in the event of an imminent CK-class reality-ending scenario, SCP-1968 could be used in a last ditch-effort to avert catastrophe

CK means restructuring of reality, which might include history, physical laws and such.

It is a highly dangerous anomaly, and 1968 might be used to counteract it.

Decided to give this another read and make no mistake, I still like this SCP but god does this have some cringey moments:

Successfully terminated SCP-354-15 and grew less active as its body cooled. After fully solidifying and having remained motionless since, subject was moved to Dr. ██████'s office for aesthetic purposes.

You would never get away with this in an SCP now. In no sane world would they put anything that came out of this pool into someone's office for aesthetic purposes

That's thrice now that we've had to fall back on Pandora's Box to deal with stuff coming out of SCP-354. Able can't complain, though… you can tell he enjoyed fighting SCP-354-11. Maybe we should set up some kind of "hotline" to MTF Ω-7?

I don't really like Able and this whole note is just cringey to me

Have you ever had a dream, where it seemed so real, but you knew you were dreaming, and it felt like you had to wake up to escape from it?

This is near enough a quote from The Matrix: "Have you ever had a dream, Neo, that you were so sure was real? What if you were unable to wake from that dream? How would you know the difference between the dream world and the real world?"

I'm going to leave my vote as is but just re-reading through this made me realise how much our standards have changed.

item.content:encoded:
Complete lurker here, so take my opinion with many grains of salt.

Even in the "EXTERMINATE MONTHLY!" old days of SCP writing, I always felt that D-Class were just filler to be used as needed. Research subjects, warm bodies, snacks for 682, whatever's needed - they're not people, they're an expendable resource.

In this case, when the first facility was set up, it was ostensibly an armed research/monitoring station. They probably kept D-Class on hand as a matter of course, just in case they needed them for an experiment or to distract an unruly monster. After the destruction of the facility and establishment of the subsequent "Murder absolutely everything that comes out of that fucking pool!" facility, they probably kept D-class on site as observers and cannon fodder. In the Foundation's position and given the increasing scale of lethality that the pool has presented, which would you rather have on the front line: armed guards or D-Class? One option will very probably result in you losing skilled personnel who will take time and money to replace in the long term, and whose loss significantly weakens your defenses in the short term. The other option allows for the facility to better plan a defensive strategy while the Bat-Faced Octopus Demon is busy trying to catch and eat screaming D-Class.

item.title: What if it isn't A portal, but a soup of many portals?
item.content:encoded:
Perhaps the thickness is not due to density of the material, but because it's filled with tiny portals, and you can't go thru more than one at the same time (the only way to get thru would be to stretch one of the portals wide enough to get thru, and their natural size is microscopic). Perhaps all the portals are inside each other (with enough spatial dimensions and non-euclidean space that should be possible), forming a sorta hyperdimensional topological sponge; and the change in density is caused by the "neck" of the wormholes? Perhaps the redness is actually the result of an anomalous relativistic effect, redshifting/blueshifting the light and radiation from all the portals together towards what we perceive as red, and because there are so many the redirections diffuses the light into the appearance of opaqueness?

And then perhaps, the exploratory log came from an alternate Foundation; and there is another Foundation that is using their end of the thing for dumping abnormals; and that place described in the log is yet another reality where they also tried to contain the pool (hence the wall).
